alternatives: The latent-order group does not reproduce a positive predictive advantage against the exact random-order expectation.
The predictive advantage is not larger in the latent-order group than in the degree-multiset-matched group.
At least one quarter of the latent-order advantage remains in the matched group, so local degree statistics or another retained property carry a material residual signal.
A matching, representation or generator control fails.

analysis.comparisonPlan: A uses independent noisy training/test tournaments sharing one explicit latent order. B samples training and test independently and uniformly from the complete labelled-tournament sets matching A's respective sorted out-degree multisets, with no shared latent order. C applies the four locked controls. Classify the dependence as supported only if A has positive advantage, A exceeds B, B retains less than one quarter of A's advantage, and every control passes. This conclusion concerns model structure only and has no physical interpretation.
analysis.stoppingRule: Execute exactly 48 paired A/B samples at each of the four declared flip counts in one primary run. After sealing, permit one deterministic reconstruction solely for byte comparison; never add samples, change the matched-null family or alter thresholds.

controls.purpose: Use the exact expectation of half the tournament edges rather than a sampled random-order baseline.
Require exact equality of the sorted vertex out-degree multisets for every paired A/B training and test object.
Require transported vertex relabelling to preserve all fitted minima and held-out scores in A and B.
Require every A test tournament to contain exactly the declared number of reversals relative to its generated latent order.

protocol.hypothesis: The held-out predictive advantage of an exact F_T-minimizing order is materially larger when training and test tournaments share an explicitly generated latent order than when both tournaments are sampled independently from uniform degree-multiset-matched null families.
